correctness.rationale: Exact path-determinant and spherical-moment formulas characterize every shadow fiber by S=x+y+z and P=xz. Real interval v=x+z from 2sqrt(P) to S parametrizes the whole fiber. The squared operator norm is max of one increasing and one decreasing branch, giving L,U with seam S=3sqrt(P). The S4 fourth power is a convex quadratic, giving Qmin,Qmax with seam S=4sqrt(P). Differentiation of normalized max/min ratios proves unique universal peaks at S/sqrt(P)=3 and 2+sqrt(2), with exact attaining matrices and no omitted edge cases. Supplementary standalone verifier executed 96164 finite assertions; not relied on for the infinite claims.

value.rationale: The natural inverse question asks how much deterministic operator norm data survives conditioning on an entire random numerical-shadow distribution. For the first four-site path with two independent shadow coefficients, the result completely quantifies sharp fiber uncertainty in two distinct norm geometries. The universal optimal discrepancies are nontrivial algebraic constants and occur at incompatible fibers, revealing a structural two-scale phenomenon, beyond isolated examples or numerical table entries.
